identity.capacity: ~15 cu ft (CONFIRMED via EnerGuide label: Type C, 13.6-15.6 cu ft band)
identity.compressor_type: induction, PTC/capacitor start not conclusively resolved from this run (100ms burst under-sampled the start transient; see electrical.plateau_a)
identity.listing: UL listed household freezer, 126A / LR7788; free-standing installation only

heat_rejection.warm_zones_observed: Warm areas felt on the FRONT, LEFT and RIGHT outer panels, HIGH UP (near the lid flange). No separate back coil. Refrigerant tubing is bonded to the outer cabinet skin; on chest freezers this band commonly also carries the anti-sweat loop around the lid flange. Either way it is hot refrigerant tubing and must stay exposed to air. Back panel not separately checked (compressor recess is there).
heat_rejection.why_it_matters: The cabinet outer skin IS the heat-rejection surface. Covering the sides is not merely inefficient -- it raises head pressure on a compressor already fighting a low refrigerant charge (see factory_spec.measured_vs_spec), lengthening runs and risking an overload trip on a 32-year-old R12 system that is not economically repairable. This is the mechanism behind the nameplate's 'free-standing installation only' listing.
heat_rejection.practical_limit: Lid-top insulation is SAFE and beneficial (see docs/outage_procedures.md section 4.2: blanket over the lid hanging only a little past the seal, plus a ~14 in folding foam mattress on top). Cabinet SIDES and the rear compressor recess must stay clear. NOTE THE MARGIN IS THIN: the warm band begins just below where the blanket edge sits, so a careless re-drape after opening the lid can cover it without being obvious.
heat_rejection.bears_on_replacement: A replacement unit should be checked for the same property. A hot-wall design constrains how much insulation can ever be added, which matters because lid insulation measurably reduces heat load -- and this freezer's high duty is THE make-or-break number in docs/rotation_budget.md.
heat_rejection.confidence: high (direct touch test by Ron while running, 2026-09-04); condenser-vs-anti-sweat attribution of the warm band is NOT resolved and does not change the handling rule
heat_rejection.source: Ron, hand check during the 2026-09-03/04 outage

identity.notes: REAL DEPLOYMENT LOAD, not a test piece. CORRECTION TO PRIOR EXPECTATION: the 5.0A nameplate is a locked-rotor-inclusive max, NOT a run-current predictor. Measured running current is ~0.72A -- consistent with the PROJECT_STATE compressor-class reasoning (~0.68A, dorm-fridge-like), and it CONTRADICTS the earlier '~1.5-2.5A running' note derived from nameplate. Current is set by compressor class, not box size. The anticipated 30-60A inrush / ACS712-clip scenario did NOT occur in the RMS-window capture (see inrush_peak_a caveat).

factory_spec.comment: Transcribed from the manufacturer performance sticker and the EnerGuide label (photos). This is the factory reference the measured data is checked against. Three independent factory figures (run-time, per-run wattage, annual kWh) all show this unit running harder than spec -- consistent with low R12 charge and/or frost-loaded evaporator on a 1994 unit.

performance_sticker.transcription_caveats: 70F high-side 95-120 and 90F high-side 130-155 were mapped from a run-together paste; column assignment for the two high-side values should be double-checked against the physical sticker.

energuide.band_position: efficient end of its similar-models band (~425 low / ~450 high)
energuide.source: EnerGuide / Consommation energetique label (photo). Units are kWh per YEAR (par annee), not per hour.

run_time_pct.delta: Measured ~70% on a normal (not 90F) bench -- over the 70F spec ceiling and at the top of the 90F range. Runs as if in a hot room while in a normal one.

per_run_wattage_w.delta: About half spec wattage. Low draw + excessive run time is the classic low-refrigerant-charge signature: too little refrigerant moved, so it never satisfies.

annual_energy_kwh.delta: ~15-18% OVER its own factory rating despite low per-run wattage, because run time is so high. A healthy unit runs less at higher per-run watts and lands at/below 425.

measured_vs_spec.frost_note: Cabinet photos show ~60-70% loose fill plus visible evaporator-wall frost buildup. Frost insulates the coil and lengthens run time -- a second mechanical contributor to high duty, on top of likely low charge. A defrost might recover some duty but won't fix charge.

factory_spec.conclusion: Three independent factory references (run-time spec, per-run wattage spec, EnerGuide annual kWh) all indicate the unit is running well beyond spec. Supports replacement. Re-characterize any replacement unit; do not inherit these numbers.

channel_binding.comment: Optional: where this load was measured/plugged during characterization. Deployment binding lives in the controller config, not here.
channel_binding.socket_label: TBD -- confirm which channel dual_logger current stream mapped to for this run

running_current_a.source: dual_logger.py merged CSV (latest_chest_freezer_run.csv), 26 complete run segments over 16.7h, steady-body mean.
running_current_a.notes: Steady running mean 0.717A. End-of-run (final 60s before thermostat cutout) averaged 0.706A, per-run range 0.673-0.788A -- FLAT into shut-off, i.e. thermostatic cutout, not a laboring/rising-current compressor. Matches dorm fridge (~0.68A) and confirms compressor-class current independence from box size.

inrush_peak_a.confidence: low -- method-limited, NOT a true surge peak
inrush_peak_a.source: max of first-3s samples across run starts, dual_logger 10Hz sample-and-hold.
inrush_peak_a.notes: 3.47A is the highest value the 10Hz/100ms-RMS-window capture saw at start; it is NOT the instantaneous inrush. A real induction-compressor start transient is sub-100ms and heavily averaged out by both the ACS712 RMS window and 10Hz sampling. True instantaneous surge is unmeasured by this rig and could be well higher (10s of amps). If a true surge number is needed for inverter sizing, capture with a scope + current shunt. Notably the feared ACS712 railing did NOT appear -- but absence of clipping here does not prove low instantaneous inrush, it reflects the averaging.

plateau_a.source: would require a fast (>=1kHz) start capture; the 100ms burst under-sampled it this run.
plateau_a.notes: Start method (PTC shelf vs capacitor/relay-start) NOT resolved. This run's start samples show current already at steady ~0.75A by the first captured point -- the settle transient fell between samples. Leaving compressor_type unresolved rather than guessing. Low priority given the replace-the-unit decision.

inrush_duration_s.notes: Current is at steady value by the first post-start sample; settle duration shorter than the sampling could resolve, OR masked by sample-and-hold. Not a limiting factor for overcurrent_trip_ms given the low steady current.

control_constants.comment: Now scaled off the MEASURED ~0.72A running current (NOT the nameplate 5.0A). These are usable starting values; confirm min_off under deliberate stress before deployment.

start_confirm_a.basis: ~half of 0.72A running; well above the ~0.10A noise floor. Same value that worked for the ~0.68A dorm fridge -- appropriate here given near-identical run current.

stop_a.basis: below run (0.72A), above noise (~0.10A), below start_confirm (0.35A) for clean hysteresis. Current collapses well past this at true cutout.

min_offer_ms.basis: start-to-steady settle is effectively immediate at this sampling; 3s offer gives ample confirm margin. Carried from dorm fridge; run-current parity justifies it.

start_debounce_ms.basis: sustained >start_confirm for 2s confirms a real run vs a stall. No large start hump observed to override this.

stop_debounce_ms.basis: current collapses cleanly at thermostat cutout; 5s confirms a genuine stop, not a momentary dip.

max_offer_ms.basis: policy. A satisfied box shows only noise -> release the slot. Unchanged from dorm fridge.

min_off_ms.confidence: must-enforce; verify under stress before deployment
min_off_ms.basis: anti-short-cycle 180s relays-open hold-off, survives resets. Run current matches the dorm PTC unit, so 180s is a reasonable floor, but this is an older/larger R12 compressor -- confirm it tolerates a hot restart at 180s before trusting it in deployment. Keep the reset hold-off enforced.

overcurrent_trip_a.basis: above legitimate steady run (0.72A, +peaks to ~0.79A end-of-run) with wide margin, below any stall. The dorm fridge's 1.5A happens to fit here BECAUSE run current is near-identical -- not because it was reused blindly. A locked-rotor event will vastly exceed this.

overcurrent_trip_ms.basis: >1.5A for >20s -> latch off. Healthy steady run never approaches 1.5A, so no false-trip risk; the start transient is far shorter than 20s. Same 20s used and validated on the dorm fridge.

thermal.comment: From RTD in freezer air (t1_freezer_f), MAX31865 + PT1000, ice-bath verified this round. Single compartment.

freezer.notes: Full observed envelope over 16.7h. Operating band held stable across the evening setpoint adjustment -- the tweak did not materially move the cycling band.

thermostat_band_f.source: mean of per-cycle ON-end minima (cut-out) and OFF-end maxima (cut-in) across ~26 cycles.
thermostat_band_f.notes: ~5F band. Full extremes ran to -7.7F / +0.8F on outlier cycles. Cycle period ~38 min, mean run ~27 min.

loading.detail: About 6 x 7 lb gel packs live in the box as deliberate thermal ballast, in addition to the food. A further 2 x 7 lb packs are shuttled to the kitchen fridge's fresh-food compartment during outages (docs/outage_procedures.md 4.3).
loading.why_it_is_recorded: EVERY drift and pulldown figure in this file is a property of THIS BOX AS LOADED, not of the freezer itself. Water-based gel is roughly 1.0 BTU/lb-F liquid and carries 144 BTU/lb of latent heat frozen, so 42 lb is a large share of the box's thermal inertia. Anyone who removed the packs to make room would quietly change the warmup rate that the whole rotation plan in docs/rotation_budget.md depends on -- with no obvious symptom until the next outage.
loading.arrangement_note: 2026-09-10: the packs were swapped end-for-end with the food (packs from the left end to the right). Watch whether the settled top/bottom gap returns to its 2-3 F baseline; if it lands elsewhere, the box's internal thermal structure changed and earlier CF readings need re-baselining before comparison.
loading.confidence: high on the count and weight (Ron); the effect on the rates is inferred, not separately measured

pulldown_rate_f_per_min.source: freezer-air slope while compressor ON, per-run segments >60s.
pulldown_rate_f_per_min.notes: WEAK. Mean cooling of only ~0.08F/min while running (best cycle ~0.26F/min). The compressor barely out-cools the cabinet heat leak -- this is WHY duty cycle is high despite low warmup. Consistent with a tired compressor and/or low R12 charge on a 1994 unit.

deployment_observation_2026_09_04.basis: REAL OUTAGE, first CF block after ~5.4 h unpowered: 22.0 F at 12:54 -> 17.0 F at 13:21 (21 min running from a warm box).
deployment_observation_2026_09_04.interpretation: NOT in conflict with the -0.075 F/min mean above. That mean was measured while cycling in the -5..0 F operating band, where compressor capacity is lowest and the leak nearly cancels it. This -0.238 F/min was taken with the box at 22 F, where capacity is far higher, and it lands right at the bench MAX of -0.261. The two agree: pulldown is strongly box-temperature-dependent and will slow sharply approaching 0 F. Treat -0.238 as an UPPER BOUND for warm-box recovery, not a constant.
deployment_observation_2026_09_04.caveat: Lid insulation (identity.heat_rejection; docs/outage_procedures.md 4.2) was added DURING this window, so the segment straddles the change. At this dT pulldown is dominated by compressor capacity rather than cabinet leak, so the effect is probably small -- but this is NOT a clean pre/post number.
deployment_observation_2026_09_04.confidence: medium (single 21-min segment, hand-read temps, insulation change mid-window)

warmup_rate_f_per_min.source: freezer-air slope while compressor OFF, per-off segments >60s.
warmup_rate_f_per_min.notes: LOW, as the chest form factor predicted (~0.18F/min vs dorm fridge's ~1.1F/min) -- big thermal mass + lid-up geometry. This is the outage-tolerance advantage and it is genuinely good. Warm-bench measurement; real cold-ambient outage would warm even slower. Note box contents/loading affects this.

deployment_observation_2026_09_04.basis: REAL OUTAGE, CF unpowered while the kitchen fridge held the inverter: 18.0 F at 11:08 -> 22.0 F at 12:54 (1.77 h). UNINSULATED -- entirely before the lid blanket/mattress went on.
deployment_observation_2026_09_04.interpretation: CONFIRMS the bench note above, emphatically. 0.038 F/min = 2.3 F/h in a real cool-house, food-loaded outage, versus the 0.184 F/min (11 F/h) warm-bench figure -- about 5x better. A rotation schedule planned against the bench number would be needlessly conservative. USE THIS ONE for outage planning; the bench figure is a lightly-loaded unit in a warm room.
deployment_observation_2026_09_04.cross_load_note: For comparison, the kitchen fridge drifted at only 0.21 F/h over the same outage (43 -> 45 F over 9.5 h overnight). The CF loses ground ~11x faster, which is the whole basis of the rotation priority in docs/outage_procedures.md 4.1.
deployment_observation_2026_09_04.supersedes_for_planning: Not the bench value itself (still valid for its conditions), but any DUTY or drift planning that assumed 0.18 F/min in an outage.
deployment_observation_2026_09_04.confidence: medium (hand-read temps, two points, single interval)

observations.ambient: indoor warm-bench (record exact ambient if available)
observations.note: Stable across the full run including the evening setpoint change.

duty_cycle.notes: MAKE-OR-BREAK PARAMETER, and it breaks. Measured ~70%, NOT the ~15-25% expected for a big-thermal-mass freezer. 3x70% is far over budget -- this unit alone nearly monopolizes a one-at-a-time rotation. The high duty is explained by the weak ~0.08F/min pulldown (see thermal): good insulation (low warmup) but a compressor that can barely hold temp. Warm-bench is a worst case and real cold-ambient Michigan outages would lower duty somewhat, BUT the low pulldown is a unit-health problem, not an ambient one. This strongly supports the replace-the-freezer decision. Re-characterize any REPLACEMENT unit before assuming rotation viability.
